question: Does Cosmo/Wanda Top 20 outperform Top 50?
summary: As of the latest Official League snapshot, Cosmo/Wanda Top 20 (Hyperliquid / USDC, dynamic MarketCapPairList, Official feed, ~1 month live) definitively outperforms Top 50 (Bitget / USDT, static 50-pair whitelist, Restarted feed, launched today). Top 20 holds league rank #3 with a net total PnL of +7.89 across 63 closed trades (+62.50 USDC realized, 100% win rate, 1.77% average ROI). Top 50 is at rank #4 with a net total PnL of -28.44 across only 9 closed trades (+6.63 USDT realized, 100% win rate, 1.35% average ROI). Top 20’s unrealized drawdown is roughly 0.9× its realized profit buffer, whereas Top 50’s is roughly 5.3× realized gains, leaving the latter structurally more vulnerable to carry-risk. Per-trade ROI, initially unstable and nominally higher for Top 50 with tiny samples, has declined to 1.35% as more trades closed, now trailing Top 20’s 1.77%. Severe confounders—different exchanges, margin currencies, dynamic vs static pairlists, and Official vs Restarted data quality—prevent an apples-to-apples strategy comparison. The operator also notes the broader Cosmo/Wanda ecosystem has ~2 years of positive live history, mostly with ~20 pairs. Conclusion: Top 20 is the clear aggregate outperformer on realized profit, throughput, total PnL, and power ranking. Reassessment is warranted once Top 50 exceeds 20 closed trades and achieves gapless Official feed continuity on a comparable exchange/currency baseline.

summary: Local indexed research (updates 215–236) finalized the step-quantum and throttling rules for the live-calibration knob X% inside Cosmo/Wanda’s immutable rank-and-floor architecture. The unit of measure is percentile points (pp), not basis points, because X% is defined as a percentile of the observed spread/ATR distribution, preserving stable population-control semantics across volatility regimes. Normal adjustments are ±1 pp per eligible cycle: tightening (−1 pp) triggers when filtered realized ROI on the X%-admissible subset drifts below the 1.5% critical lower bound (with throughput above the 20-pair hard floor), or when throughput sits above the 30-pair buffer and ROI comfortably exceeds the ~1.75–1.79% incumbent baseline; loosening (+1 pp) triggers when throughput is healthy (≥25 pairs) and ROI exceeds baseline. Emergency quanta are +5 pp for emergency loosening (or to the 70th percentile, whichever is smaller), triggered immediately when pass-through drops below the 20-pair hard floor, and −2 pp for emergency tightening, triggered when filtered ROI sags below 1.5% and the downtrend is accelerating. Five anti-oscillation layers throttle consecutive steps: (1) in-cycle lock permitting only one X% adjustment per dispersion-rank refresh cycle; (2) hysteresis confirmation requiring a threshold breach to persist for two consecutive telemetry readings (two rank-refresh cycles) before acting; (3) directional reversal lock preventing loosening after a tightening until pass-through ≥25 pairs and filtered ROI ≥1.75% for one full cycle, and vice versa; (4) a daily delta cap bounding net movement to ±3 pp within any rolling 24-hour window; and (5) hard bounds preventing X% from loosening beyond the 50th percentile or tightening beyond the 95th percentile. Operationally, at the 75th–80th percentile anchor a normal ±1 pp move is expected to shift pass-through by roughly 1–3 pairs on a Top 50 universe, while the +5 pp emergency loosening is sized to lift pass-through from sub-20 into the 22–26 pair range in one action. The two-cycle hysteresis ensures temporary dips to 1.49% ROI or 19.5 effective pairs do not trigger immediate reactions; only sustained drift does.

question: What warm-start and crash-recovery protocol should the external telemetry controller use to restore hysteresis counters, rolling 24-hour delta budgets, and last-known X% across restarts without breaching the daily ±3 pp cap or replaying steps?
summary: The external telemetry controller—owner of the step state machine enforcing a daily ±3 pp rolling-window cap, 2-reading hysteresis with a directional reversal lock, and authoritative X% persisted at every rank-refresh cycle—must implement a seven-point crash-recovery contract. (1) Atomic Snapshot Contract: at the end of every rank-refresh cycle, atomically write a warm-state blob to the config store alongside authoritative X%. The blob must contain x_percent_authoritative, hysteresis_counter, last_direction, directional_lock_until, an append-only rolling_delta_log of {timestamp, delta_signed_pp} retained for at least 24 hours, a denormalized daily_delta_consumed sum, bound_exhaustion_flags, manual_override_active (plus a clamped override value), and last_processed_telemetry_ts. (2) Cold-Boot Reload Sequence: on restart, before opening the telemetry loop, load the warm-state blob; if absent or unreadable, fall back to the initial live calibration X% with a full 3 pp budget and hysteresis counter set to 0. Restore x_percent_authoritative directly into memory—never recompute from raw telemetry history or replay steps. Rehydrate the rolling 24-hour budget by scanning rolling_delta_log, discarding entries older than (restart_time − 24 h), and recomputing daily_delta_consumed as the sum of absolute surviving deltas. Restore hysteresis, last direction, and reinstate any future directional lock. If bound-exhaustion flags are set, disable auto-stepping in that direction and emit a CRITICAL BOUND_EXHAUST_RESTORE event. If a manual override is active, clamp it to hard bounds, apply immediately, pause auto-stepping, and log OVERRIDE_RESTORED. (3) Hysteresis Warmth Without Replay: the restored hysteresis counter resumes at its saved value but is advanced only by fresh post-restart telemetry readings. The controller must not synthesize readings from the outage gap. On the first fresh cycle: if the reading aligns with last_direction, increment the counter; if it contradicts, reset to 1 in the new direction (or 0 on neutral). This ensures a post-crash spike cannot single-handedly trigger a step. (4) Idempotency and No-Replay Guarantee: rolling_delta_log is used exclusively for budget accounting and is never reapplied to mutate X% on reload. The authoritative X% is taken solely from x_percent_authoritative in the blob. On the first fresh cycle, emit a structured WARM_START telemetry record (restored X%, hysteresis count, remaining budget, lock status, bound flags, override state) to create an auditable checkpoint. (5) Mid-Cycle Crash Safety: if the controller crashes before completing the atomic snapshot, the next boot loads the previous cycle’s committed blob. Because the truncated cycle never wrote a new delta or updated the hysteresis counter, the state is inherently safe: the uncommitted step is lost, which is correct behavior (no replay). The 24-hour budget is unchanged because the delta was never appended. (6) Daily Cap Exhaustion on Restart: if rehydration shows daily_delta_consumed ≥ 3.0 pp, the controller enters DELTA_CAP_EXHAUSTED state. All auto-steps are blocked; telemetry observation and logging continue. Any emergency signal triggers a CONFLICT event and a manual-review alert. The controller exits this state only when aged-out log entries free headroom or a human sets x_percent_manual_override. (7) Downstream Pairlist Consistency: the strategy class remains agnostic to calibration. The Freqtrade pairlist callback (RemotePairList) reads X% from the same config store. To minimize drift during controller restart, the reload routine immediately republishes the restored x_percent_authoritative to the config store with a warm_start timestamp, ensuring the callback picks up the authoritative value on its next refresh cycle rather than operating on a stale gate.

question: What schema, versioning, and atomic-write semantics should the config-store persistence layer use to guarantee that the warm-state blob and authoritative X% are committed together without torn writes, and how should the controller validate blob integrity on reload?
summary: The research established that the warm-state blob and authoritative X% must be stored as a single indivisible artifact using a monolithic envelope-payload schema (exactly one JSON document or equivalent DB row). The envelope carries schema_version (monotonic integer), cycle_seq (monotonic integer/ULID per rank-refresh cycle), written_at (ISO-8601 timestamp), and checksum (SHA-256 over canonical payload serialization). The payload nests x_percent_authoritative together with all step-state machine fields—hysteresis_counter, last_direction, directional_lock_until, append-only rolling_delta_log, denormalized daily_delta_consumed, bound_exhaustion_flags, manual_override_active/value, and last_processed_telemetry_ts—to eliminate multi-key divergence. Schema versioning is guarded by a controller-side MAX_SUPPORTED_SCHEMA constant; if the loaded blob exceeds it, the controller falls back to initial live calibration X% with a full 3 pp budget and hysteresis counter 0. Cycle versioning uses monotonic cycle_seq to reject stale or rollbacked blobs. Atomic-write semantics are store-type specific: file-backed stores write to a temp file, fsync, then atomically rename; key/value stores use a single-key PUT or compare-and-swap; relational stores upsert a single row holding the full payload plus envelope columns inside an explicit transaction. On reload, the controller runs a strict five-gate validation chain before opening the telemetry loop: Gate A checks readability and SHA-256 checksum; Gate B checks schema_version ≤ MAX_SUPPORTED_SCHEMA; Gate C checks cycle_seq monotonicity and that written_at is not in the future; Gate D asserts mandatory field completeness and range sanity, clamping out-of-bounds X% to hard limits and continuing rather than falling back; Gate E scans rolling_delta_log, discards entries older than restart_time − 24 h, recomputes the absolute sum, and overwrites daily_delta_consumed if the discrepancy exceeds epsilon (0.001 pp). After passing all gates, the controller restores x_percent_authoritative directly into memory without replaying telemetry or recomputing from history, immediately republishes the restored value to the config store with a warm_start timestamp (and fresh cycle_seq if republishing), and emits a structured WARM_START telemetry record for auditability.

summary: The warm-state persistence layer must expose a four-domain operational surface built atop the indexed five-gate validation chain (Gates A–E) and the monolithic envelope-payload atomic-persistence contract. (1) Telemetry: emit a structured WARM_START record after every successful reload capturing restored x_percent_authoritative, hysteresis count, remaining 24-hour delta budget, directional lock, bound-exhaustion flags, and override state; emit first-class gate-level outcome events (BLOB_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH for Gate A, SCHEMA_VERSION_REJECT for Gate B, STALE_ROLLBACK_REJECT for Gate C, BLOB_INTEGRITY_CLAMP for Gate D, DELTA_LOG_RECOMPUTED for Gate E); and expose write-path counters for atomic-staging latency and incomplete staging attempts. (2) Alerting: Gate A failures trigger a critical torn-write alert carrying cycle_seq, written_at, and checksums; two consecutive fallbacks to initial live calibration escalate to PERSISTENCE_POISONED and force a clean initial-calibration boot; SCHEMA_VERSION_REJECT is wired to deployment dashboards; STALE_ROLLBACK_REJECT is wired to an operational channel for clock-skew or tampering detection. (3) Schema-migration tooling: an in-place additive migration shim keyed by monotonic schema_version injects safe defaults for missing payload keys when the loaded blob is ≤ MAX_SUPPORTED_SCHEMA but older than the writer’s version; a forward-compatibility guard enforces schema_version ≤ MAX_SUPPORTED_SCHEMA or triggers safe fallback; a dual-version write window maintains both previous and current envelope versions during a schema bump; and a read-only metadata endpoint advertises MAX_SUPPORTED_SCHEMA and the last committed blob’s schema_version. (4) Remediation automation: atomic staging (tmp + fsync + rename, CAS, or single-row upsert) prevents torn writes by construction; if Gate A still fails, the controller falls back to initial calibration, starts a fresh rolling delta log, and overwrites the corrupt artifact after the next rank refresh; repeated failures on the same stored blob cause it to be discarded and bootstrapped from scratch; old blobs are migrated in-memory by the shim, while forward-incompatible blobs trigger the safe fallback path instead of a parse error.

question: What differentiates the profitable live strategies (Cosmo & Wanda and Timmy Top 50) from the underperforming development league candidates (Downforce, Jade) when cross-referencing shift review rubrics, backtest JSON metrics, and live trading diagnostics indexed in the local corpus?
summary: The local corpus identifies six stacked architectural dimensions that separate profitable live strategies (Cosmo & Wanda Top 50 and Timmy Top 50) from underperforming development candidates (Downforce and Jade). (1) Throughput Calibration (Behavior Fit): Live strategies sustain sustainable trade frequency (~5.4–11.5 closed trades per 24h), whereas Downforce (64.5/24h) and Jade (84.6/24h) violently exceed the aggressive mandate ceiling of 16.0/24h, scoring only 4.0/25 on Behavior Fit. (2) Entry Quality & Multi-Timeframe Confirmation (Economics): Cosmo/Wanda employs a stacked confirmation model—Ichimoku cloud alignment across 5m–8h, FGI-scaled fan-magnitude gain, EMA trend stacks, ADX/DI spread, volume spike confirmation, and directional candle consensus—while Timmy adds a pre-expansion compression layer (t_* indicators, low-gap bucket, climate temp, conviction scores) that filters Cosmo signals. This yields positive expectancy (Cosmo Top 50: 100% win rate, +2.49% avg ROI, +65.42 realized PnL; Timmy Top 50: +17.08 realized, best trade +19.37%). In contrast, Downforce shows negative expectancy (-0.12%/trade) on a 25% win rate and Jade shows -0.14%/trade on a 29% win rate; shift diagnostics explicitly flag 'entries are low quality' and recommend adding trend/volatility/volume confirmation—the exact layers live strategies already enforce. (3) Exit Discipline & Payoff Asymmetry: Cosmo/Wanda uses profit-only exits, dynamic ROI engines, champion trailing stops, and partial siphoning, allowing winners to run (best closed trade +15.17%). Timmy v3 compresses open exposure to a single ticket to prevent loser drag and achieves extreme positive skew (best +19.37% vs worst open ~-0.6%), earning a trust score of 85.0 with Clean data quality. Cosmo & Wanda Top 50, despite a 100% closed-trade win rate, carries significant open-position risk (unrealized drag of -41.89 consuming ~64% of realized profits, worst open -16.49%), contributing to a lower trust score of 45.0 and a Restarted data-quality flag. Conversely, Jade exhibits catastrophic payoff asymmetry: winners average +0.09% while losers average -0.23% (payoff ratio 0.37). Downforce's custom exit 'df_short_exit' bled -2.39. Shift mutation briefs for both candidates call for rebalancing exits—raising ROI targets and shortening loss stops—inverting their current framework toward the live strategies' 'let winners breathe, cut losers' model. (4) Structural Risk Gating & Regime Brakes: Cosmo Top 50 records 0% max drawdown with 44–47 consecutive wins. Its config enforces a slot-ladder extremity gate (slots 4–9 require green-count and winner-threshold proofs) and a delayed ignition system that pauses over-deployment until baseline PnL moves by 3–6%. Downforce suffered five consecutive losses with 'no regime brake,' and Jade had a worst-open excursion of -1.0% with consistent pair drag (ZEC/USDC). Neither implements the ignition threshold or gating ladder present in live configs. (5) Universe Discipline & Infrastructure Maturity: Live strategies run on standardized, liquid static pairlists (Top 20/50/100 marketcap) via Binance USDT futures with 5m timeframes, consistent 1x leverage, and well-defined portfolio size (max_open_trades 18). Backtest JSONs show deliberate universe_key alignment and StaticPairList discipline. Development candidates rely on bespoke, ill-defined universes—Downforce's 'custom wind-tunnel' and Jade's 'BTC + Top 20 basket'—leading to liquidity mismatches and pair-specific drag. (6) Rubric Decomposition: Downforce and Jade both scored 46.9/100 (Grade D). Their rubrics show high Reliability (~17.9/20) but collapsed Behavior Fit (4.0/25) and Economics (3.0/30). Cosmo & Wanda and Timmy live metrics imply Economics scores near ceiling. The live strategies' superior Economics and Behavior Fit are driven by the confirmation layers and exit engines that development league reviews now mandate as fixes. Conclusion: The live strategies differentiate through a stacked edge—calibrated frequency, multi-horizon entry confirmation, asymmetric payoff control, and mechanical regime brakes. The underperforming candidates lack these layers, resulting in over-traded, negatively skewed, low-conviction execution despite occasional superficial signals.
